content-first-instance-of-abbreviation-n.title: First instance of abbreviation not expanded

page-layout-wide-page-forces-users-to-sc.title: Wide page forces users to scroll horizontally

colour-and-contrast-colour-alone-is-used.title: Colour alone is used to convey content

wcag.rationale: Edible versus poisonous is conveyed only by red/green text colour (the two colours differ by 1.12:1).

colour-and-contrast-small-text-does-not-.title: Small text does not have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 so does not meet AA

wcag.rationale: 12px #757980 on white is 4.37:1, below 4.5:1.
4.37:1 is also below the 7:1 enhanced threshold.

colour-and-contrast-large-text-does-not-.title: Large text does not have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 so does not meet AA

wcag.rationale: 20px normal-weight #878c8c on white is 3.41:1; 20px is not large text under WCAG, so the 4.5:1 threshold applies and fails.
3.41:1 is below the enhanced threshold.

colour-and-contrast-large-text-does-not-.notes: Fixture flaw: the "large" text is 20px (15pt) normal weight, which WCAG does not count as large text; it would pass 3:1 if it were large.

colour-and-contrast-small-text-does-not-.title: Small text does not have a contrast ratio of at least 7:1 so does not meet AAA

wcag.rationale: 12px #9499a1 on white is 2.86:1, below 7:1.
2.86:1 is also below the AA threshold of 4.5:1.

colour-and-contrast-small-text-does-not-.notes: Fixture flaw: intended to pass AA and fail AAA, but at 2.86:1 it fails AA too.

colour-and-contrast-large-text-does-not-.title: Large text does not have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 so does not meet AAA

20px normal text is not large text, so 3.41:1 also fails 4.5:1.

colour-and-contrast-large-text-does-not-.notes: Fixture flaw: uses class low-contrast-large-aa instead of low-contrast-large-aaa, so it is identical to the AA large-text case; neither is large text by the WCAG definition.

colour-and-contrast-focus-not-visible.title: Focus not visible

wcag.rationale: The button's focus style swaps a 2px border for a 1px border plus 1px outline; an indicator exists but is weak (borderline).
The focus indicator change is at most about 1px thick, well short of the 2 CSS px perimeter area with 3:1 change contrast.

colour-and-contrast-focus-not-visible.notes: Title says focus is "not visible", but the CSS draws a thin outline; mapped to 2.4.13 rather than 2.4.7.

typography-blink-element-found.title: Blink element found

typography-italics-used-on-long-sections.title: Italics used on long sections of text

wcag.rationale: display:none removes "about football" from the accessible name, leaving "Read more" with no context on the page.
The link text alone is "Read more".

css-page-zoom-boxes-that-dont-expand-wit.title: Page zoom - boxes that don't expand with the text

wcag.rationale: The box has fixed height 4.2em and overflow hidden while its width is 50 %, so at 200 % zoom wrapped text is clipped.
At 320 CSS px the 50 % wide fixed-height box clips text; likely a reflow failure (borderline: depends on rendering).
Increased text spacing would overflow the fixed height.

html-duplicate-id.title: Duplicate id

wcag.rationale: Two elements have id="nav".

html-duplicate-id.notes: Only fails 4.1.1 (removed in 2.2); no ID reference uses "nav", so 1.3.1 and 4.1.2 are unaffected.

html-article-element-used-to-mark-up-an-.title: Article element used to mark-up an element that's not an article/blog post etc.

wcag.rationale: An article element wraps related navigation, which misrepresents structure slightly (F43 pattern, borderline).
An empty p is not exposed by AT and creates no barrier.
<center> is obsolete but renders centred text with no accessibility impact.
role="breadcrumbs" is not a valid ARIA role; browsers fall back to the native ol list role, so semantics survive.

html-object-not-embedded-accessibly-wmod.title: Object not embedded accessibly - wmode parameter not set to window

wcag.rationale: The wmode parameter concerned Flash plugin keyboard access, which no longer exists; the object has fallback text.
The spacer GIF has alt="", which is correct for decoration; using images for layout is outdated practice only.
Foreground colour is set without a background colour (F24 pattern); blue on white is 8.6:1, so it fails only if users change background.

html-start-and-close-tags-dont-match.title: Start and close tags don't match

wcag.rationale: A stray closes an element that was never opened.

html-start-and-close-tags-dont-match.notes: Only fails 4.1.1, which is removed in WCAG 2.2.

html-pre-element-without-code-element-in.title: PRE element without CODE element inside it

wcag.rationale: ASCII art inside the pre element has no text alternative.
Using pre for preformatted text is fine; no code element is required.
<font> is obsolete but has no accessibility effect beyond the visual style it sets.
